subject: Archaeology
title: Pavlopetri: Walking on a Sunken Town
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pavlopetri: Walking on a Sunken Town.

hook.text: The oldest known submerged city sits in just 12 feet of water off southern Greece. You can swim right over it.

buildup.text: Pavlopetri dates to 2800 BCE and has streets, houses, tombs, and a possible town square — all on the seabed.

discovery.text: Nicholas Flemming discovered it in 1967 while snorkeling. He spotted walls and realized they were man-made.

twist.text: Earthquakes around 1000 BCE submerged it. The seabed preserved walls that erosion on land would have destroyed long ago.

climax.text: 3D digital mapping in 2009 revealed a complete Bronze Age town plan — the most detailed ever found underwater.

punchline.text: A 5,000-year-old town sits in snorkeling depth. History is twelve feet down.

quiz.question: What makes Pavlopetri archaeologically unique?
options: It is the deepest submerged city ever discovered
It is the oldest known submerged city in the world
It contains the only underwater temple ever found
